from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
import math

def solve(n: int) -> QuantumCircuit:
    qc = QuantumCircuit(n)
    dim = 1 << n
    state = [0.0] * dim
    amp = 1.0 / math.sqrt(n)
    # |1...0> with the 1 on qubit i  -> index 1<<i  (little endian)
    for i in range(n):
        state[1 << i] = amp
    qc.initialize(state, qc.qubits)
    return qc

from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit.circuit.library import WState


def solve(n: int) -> QuantumCircuit:
    qc = QuantumCircuit(n)
    # WState prepares |W_n> = 1/sqrt(n) sum_i |0...010...0>
    # from the |0>^n state, which is a fundamentally different
    # construction from the manual Ry / initialize approaches.
    qc.compose(WState(n), inplace=True)
    return qc

from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit.circuit.library import DickeState


def solve(n: int) -> QuantumCircuit:
    qc = QuantumCircuit(n)
    # Dicke(n, k=1) == W_n = 1/sqrt(n) sum_i |0...010...0>
    # The state is symmetric under permutation of the qubits, so it
    # coincides with
    # 1/sqrt(n)(|10..0> + |010..0> + ... + |0..01>).
    qc.append(DickeState(n, 1), qc.qubits)
    return qc

from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit.circuit.library import StatePreparation
import math


def solve(n: int) -> QuantumCircuit:
    qc = QuantumCircuit(n)

    amp = 1.0 / math.sqrt(n)
    dim = 1 << n
    # little endian: basis |1 0 ... 0> is index 1<<i
    state = [0.0] * dim
    for i in range(n):
        state[1 << i] = amp

    prep = StatePreparation(state)
    qc.compose(prep, inplace=True)
    return qc
